rows.why: Item 10 asks which time zone and which day decide that it is Monday. The pick formats the instant as a weekday in the given zone, so 16:30Z counts as Monday in Singapore and 15:59:59Z still counts as Sunday.
The DST case is the same question about which local day decides Monday. Formatting the weekday in America/New_York follows the shifted offset, so 04:30Z is Monday and 03:59:59Z is Sunday.

The specific thing this scenario settles beyond basic listing is the furthest gate when there are no submissions. Item 8 picks gate 0 and otherwise the highest gate, which matches. Items 4 (merged excluded) and 7 (age) also touch it, but item 8 is the closest fit.
Item 7 asks how age is computed and in what unit. The pick counts whole 24-hour periods rounded down, which gives 9 for 9d23h and 10 for exactly 10d.

The main rule is the stall threshold and whether the boundary counts. Item 1 picks >= 14×24h, so exactly 14 days is stalled and 13d23h is not. Items 2 and 3 (posting fallback, latest submission) also agree with the rest of the scenario.
Item 6 asks for the list order. The pick puts stalled tasks first, then oldest posted first, then id ascending, which matches the scenario.
Item 9 asks what the subject says and how it handles a count of 1. The pick always writes the plural 'tasks', but the scenario expects '1 open task'.
Item 5 asks what the digest returns when nothing is open. The pick returns null rather than an empty digest, which matches 'no digest at all'.
Item 11 asks what happens with an unknown time zone. The pick throws an Error naming the zone, which matches the scenario.
